summary: The regulars want a slate: {regular} says the people who gather at your work should run their own slate for {the body}, with you on it.
realLife: He ran a tailor shop in Greeneville, Tennessee, where locals argued politics while he worked. In 1829 he and friends put up a ticket of working men and he was elected to the town board.
gates: Your job record puts you where the public comes in.

weights: How many regulars you have ties with.
Your household's income and line of work.

branches.then: Hosting the meetings costs you customers who back the other side, and the lost business shows up later.
Your boss says no politics on the clock. Joining means meeting somewhere else, or risking the job.
